english: Strange markings cover the cave walls.
Painted in faded pigments.
Humanoid figures. Simple. Primitive.
Red and white against the dark stone.
Multiple figures depicted across several surfaces.
(Examine the paintings.)
(Touch the paint.)
You step closer to inspect them.
The style is... unsettling.
Crude stick figures with circular heads.
Arms spread wide.
Some kind of ritual or dance.
You reach out carefully.
The pigment is dry. Ancient.
But still vibrant somehow.
Preserved by the cave conditions.
The goblin shrugs.
Cave art. Seen some before.
These look older than most though.
He's right.
The primitive cave paintings stare back at you.
Ancient humanoid figures frozen in their eternal dance.
(Count the figures.)
Analyze the paintings' age and origin.
These look human.
E-Fascinating. But I should move on.
You scan across the walls.
Three distinct figures. Each a unique design.
These are old.
Older than the Whitemane ruins.
Probably from the Fade Era.
When the snailfolk ruled these lands.
Before Norvik. Before humanity.
But that's just a guess.
Dating cave paintings is difficult without proper study.
Indestructible. Yes, perhaps.
(Run your hand over the paint again.)
There appears to be a layer of protection around each part of the paintings. Most of the rock itself, too.
A spell above Jor's Limit protects them.
They've survived. Perfectly.
No fading. No degradation.
Despite what should be millennia of exposure.
That's... very esoteric.
Quite so.
They do.
Humanoid at least.
Two arms. Two legs. Round head.
But the style is too simple to determine species.
Could be human. Could be something else.
Goblins?
He laughs.
We weren't even on this continent when these were made.
My guess would be... pre-Fade maybe?
Pre-Fade?
Before the Fade Era?
That would make these incredibly ancient.
You study the figures carefully.
The pigments. The style. The preservation.
It's not Whitemane nor snailfolk in origin.
These paintings predate all of them.
Before the snailfolk?
Yes.
Before the Fade Era. At the earliest, these should be dated to the early Gate Wars.
Long before recorded human history.
They do look quite alien. What are those creatures supposed to be even?
They could be depictions of a forgotten Beast of Jor.
A folktype or higher being connected with Jor.
Though the less exciting answer would be: these are rare aberrations, depicted by whatever people inhabited Askan before the Toulin'catl.
I choose to believe these are super interesting alien artwork that just happens to be left here below the city.
M-I should... document this.
Their interest is another clue to their origin.
Whatever the Golden Horde must think important enough to send an Ambassador to spelunk for must have some inherent value.
Unless the celestials happen to be idiots. Which is not a possibility to forgo.
You already are.
(Look down at your hands.)
Pencil in hand, you see a scribble depicting these three figures, along with all the strange lettering.
Didn't know you were an art-connoisseur, Cleric, your companion says, looking over your sketches.
Which one of the three do you like the most?
The left one.
The middle one.
The right one.
Hm. Why?
Six legs. Like a spider. It's cool.
Looks stable.
I think I could have a nice conversation with that one.
Six arms. I wish I had six arms.
The head design looks neat. Like a singular focus inside the mind of an alien god.
Looks spicy.
Because look at it- are those horns? Eye-stalks? Two giant erections? We just don't know. Mystery makes the man.
Broad-legged son-of-a-bitch. Nothing could topple that stance.
He looks like he could need a hug.
The goblin laughs at your justification.
I can see that. I'll pick the same.
E-Right. (Put away your sketches and leave.)
